name: Bikkurim Declaration (Viduy Bikkurim)
notes: The recitation of Deuteronomy 26:3-10 accompanying the bringing of first fruits; who recites and who does not (convert, guardian, slave, woman, tumtum, androginus)

name: Eligibility to Bring Bikkurim
notes: Who brings and recites, who brings but does not recite, and who does not bring at all — including sharecroppers, robbers, converts, women, slaves, guardians

name: Bikkurim from the Seven Species
notes: Requirement that bikkurim come specifically from the seven species; restrictions on produce from hills, valleys, or non-choice olives

name: Bikkurim Pilgrimage Procession
notes: The festive procession of bringing bikkurim to Jerusalem — the maamad assemblies, the ox with gilded horns, the flute, the greeting by Temple officials

name: Waving of Bikkurim (Tenufah)
notes: The ritual waving of the bikkurim basket by the owner and priest together at the Temple

name: Additions to Bikkurim (Tosfet Bikkurim)
notes: Laws of produce added to bikkurim baskets beyond the bikkurim themselves, and the ornamentation of bikkurim — their status and rules

name: Designation of Bikkurim (Hekdesh bikkurim)
notes: The act of marking first fruits while still attached to the soil; the dispute whether a second designation is required after plucking

name: Bikkurim as Priestly Property
notes: Status of bikkurim as priest's property — may be used to purchase slaves, land, or unclean animals; distribution to mishmar

name: Convert's Bikkurim and Declaration
notes: Convert brings bikkurim but cannot recite the declaration ('which the Lord swore to our fathers'); prayer formulations for converts in synagogue vs. private

name: Comparative Halakhic Analysis (X is like Y in some ways)
notes: The Mishnaic literary form of comparing legal categories (terumah vs. bikkurim, etrog vs. tree/vegetable, koy vs. behemah/hayyah, androginus vs. man/woman) to derive halakha

name: Koy (Animal of Uncertain Classification)
notes: The koy is an animal of uncertain status — neither clearly domesticated (behemah) nor wild (hayyah); its laws regarding blood covering, chelev, firstborn, kilayim, and shechitah

name: Etrog's Halakhic Classification
notes: The etrog is compared to both a tree and a vegetable — implications for orlah, revai, shemitah, and tithing by harvest time vs. growth time

name: Androginus (Hermaphrodite) — Detailed Halakhic Status
notes: Comprehensive treatment of the androginus: ways it is like a man, like a woman, like both, and like neither — covering tumah, inheritance, mitzvot, testimony, yibbum, nazirite vows

name: Ma'amad (Assembly for Temple Pilgrimage)
notes: The cities of the maamad would assemble together and travel jointly to Jerusalem for bikkurim; the maamad officer's role

name: Tumah Status of Human Blood
notes: Human blood compared to animal blood (renders seeds susceptible to tumah) and to sheretz blood (not liable for eating) — its dual halakhic nature

name: Owner's Responsibility for Bikkurim Until Delivery
notes: The owner bears financial/halakhic responsibility for bikkurim from designation until arrival at the Temple Mount; replacement obligations if lost, stolen, or became impure

name: Bikkurim and the Onen
notes: An onen (mourner before burial) is forbidden from eating bikkurim; dispute of R. Shimon who permits

name: Biur Bikkurim (Removal of Bikkurim)
notes: Bikkurim are subject to the law of biur (removal); dispute whether this applies equally or is exempted per R. Shimon
